## [Waste-to-energy and cross-cutting approvals]{.en}[垃圾焚烧及通用审批]{.zh}

::: {.en}
**A Victorian WtE plant needs four separate approvals, and a Chinese SOE needs approvals in both countries. That is why CDEG should enter as a contractor to a licence holder, not as an owner.**

Recycling Victoria became EPA Victoria's Circular Economy division in mid-2026, so one regulator now handles the cap licence and the environmental licences \[43\] [to verify]{.verify} (exact date). The owner holds the project approvals. The operator shares duties under the permitted-waste rules, ash handling and SOCI, and CDEG needs its own corporate approvals at the bottom of Table 2.

**Table 2. Approvals for a thermal WtE plant in Victoria, and who holds them**

::: tw
| Approval | Body and law | What it tests | Holder | For CDEG |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cap licence | EPA Circular Economy division; *Circular Economy (Waste Reduction and Recycling) Act 2021* | Nearness to feedstock and offtake, viability, permits held, jobs, energy output, fit and proper person, climate impact \[43\] | Owner | 94% allocated; the government does not support raising the cap again \[30\] [to verify]{.verify} |
| EPA development, then operating licence | EPA; *Environment Protection Act 2017*; guideline 1559.1 | Best available techniques; EU BAT is the practical reference (Appendix C) \[46\]. EPA tied Laverton North's approval to European limits \[2\] | Owner (operator named) | CDEG's emissions record supports the owner's case |
| Planning permit | Council or Minister for Planning | Siting, traffic, community. No minimum buffer distance \[7\] | Owner | Main social-licence hurdle (4.4) |
| Federal referral | DCCEEW; *EPBC Act* | Matters of national environmental significance | Owner | Site-specific |
| Grid connection | AEMO and network owner | Connection studies, queue | Owner | Easier at former coal sites (3.1e) |
| Permitted-waste rules | WtE Scheme scope guidance | No recyclables; deposit containers banned in any amount; commercial waste must pass the "not practicable to recycle" test \[36\] | Owner and operator | Needs sorting before the furnace (3.3) |
| Ash | EPA, case by case | Bottom ash: testing before use as aggregate. Fly ash: hazardous, needs treatment and licensed disposal \[7\] [to verify]{.verify} | Owner and operator | CDEG reuses 100% of its slag and stabilises fly ash before landfill; resource routes for fly ash are in development \[3\] |
| Foreign investment | FIRB; *Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Act 1975* | An SOE is a foreign government investor: \$0 threshold, and starting an Australian business needs approval \[16\] | CDEG | A Melbourne entity triggers FIRB. A service contract signed from China may not [to verify]{.verify} (legal advice) |
| Critical infrastructure | Home Affairs; *SOCI Act 2018* | Risk-management programs for owners of critical water and energy assets; duties pass to contractors \[55\] | Owner, passed to contractor | CDEG must pass the owner's supplier and personnel checks |
| China-side outbound approvals | NDRC (Order No. 49, from 1 Dec 2026), MOFCOM, SAFE, Chengdu SASAC \[17\] | Outbound investment and foreign-exchange filing | CDEG | Needed for a Melbourne entity and any parent guarantee |
:::

**The rules are tightening.** The parliamentary inquiry (August 2026) made 59 findings and 33 recommendations \[7\]. Four matter most for an operator:

-   continuous emissions monitoring with real-time public reporting (Recommendation 22)
-   international best-practice standards written into regulation (Recommendation 19)
-   flexible council supply contracts (Recommendation 12)
-   a review of whether economic incentives still favour recycling (Recommendation 13), which could mean a WtE levy

The government has six months to respond, so its response is due around February 2027 \[7\]. The state election on 28 November 2026 comes first \[8\].

**So what for CDEG.** As a contractor, CDEG carries little of the project-approval risk. It needs the corporate approvals (FIRB for its entity and the China-side filings) and must meet the owner's SOCI risk-management duties. In return, its emissions data must meet the bar the inquiry has set.
:::

::: {.zh}
**一座维州焚烧电厂需要四项单独的审批，而一家中国国企还需要两国的审批。因此，集团应以许可持有方承包商的身份进入，而不是以业主身份进入。**

Recycling Victoria已于2026年年中并入维州EPA，成为其循环经济部门，因此现在由同一监管机构负责配额许可和环境许可 \[43\] [待核实]{.verify}（具体日期）。项目审批由业主持有。运营方在准入垃圾规则、灰渣处理和SOCI方面承担共同义务，集团还需要表2底部所列的公司层面审批。

**表2：维州热处理焚烧电厂所需审批及持有方**

::: tw
| 审批 | 机构与法律 | 审查内容 | 持有方 | 对集团的意义 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 配额许可 | EPA循环经济部门；《2021年循环经济（减废与回收）法》 | 与原料和产品市场的距离、可行性、已持有的许可、就业、能源产出、适当人选审查、气候影响 \[43\] | 业主 | 已分配94%；政府不支持再次提高上限 \[30\] [待核实]{.verify} |
| EPA开发许可，之后为运营许可 | EPA；《2017年环境保护法》；指南1559.1 | 最佳可行技术；欧盟BAT是实际参照（附录C）\[46\]。EPA将Laverton North的批准与欧洲限值挂钩 \[2\] | 业主（需指定运营方） | 集团的排放记录可支持业主的申请 |
| 规划许可 | 市政或规划部长 | 选址、交通、社区。没有最低缓冲距离要求 \[7\] | 业主 | 社会许可的主要障碍（4.4） |
| 联邦转介 | 联邦气候变化、能源、环境和水务部；《EPBC法》 | 具有国家环境意义的事项 | 业主 | 视场址而定 |
| 并网 | AEMO和电网所有者 | 接入研究、排队 | 业主 | 燃煤电厂旧址更容易（3.1e） |
| 准入垃圾规则 | 焚烧发电计划范围指南 | 不得含可回收物；押金回收容器无论多少一律禁止；工商业垃圾必须通过“无法合理回收”测试 \[36\] | 业主和运营方 | 入炉前需要分拣（3.3） |
| 灰渣 | EPA，逐案审批 | 炉渣：作为骨料使用前须检测。飞灰：属危险废物，需处理并在有许可的场所处置 \[7\] [待核实]{.verify} | 业主和运营方 | 集团炉渣100%资源化利用，飞灰稳定化后填埋；飞灰资源化路线正在开发中 \[3\] |
| 外国投资 | FIRB；《1975年外国收购与接管法》 | 国企属于外国政府投资者：门槛为0澳元，在澳洲开展新业务需要批准 \[16\] | 集团 | 设立墨尔本实体须经FIRB审批。从国内签订服务合同可能不需要 [待核实]{.verify}（需法律意见） |
| 关键基础设施 | 内政部；《2018年关键基础设施安全法》（SOCI） | 关键水务和能源资产所有者须建立风险管理计划；义务传递给承包商 \[55\] | 业主，传递给承包商 | 集团必须通过业主对供应商和人员的审查 |
| 国内境外投资审批 | 国家发改委（第49号令，2026年12月1日起施行）、商务部、外汇局、成都市国资委 \[17\] | 境外投资和外汇备案 | 集团 | 设立墨尔本实体及提供母公司担保时需要 |
:::

**规则正在收紧。** 议会调查（2026年8月）提出59项结论和33项建议 \[7\]。对运营方最重要的有四项：

-   连续排放监测并实时公开报告（第22项建议）
-   将国际最佳实践标准写入法规（第19项建议）
-   灵活的市政供应合同（第12项建议）
-   审查经济激励是否仍有利于回收（第13项建议），这可能意味着征收焚烧税

政府须在六个月内回应，因此预计约2027年2月发布 \[7\]。2026年11月28日的州选举在此之前 \[8\]。

**对集团的意义：** 作为承包商，集团承担的项目审批风险很小。集团需要公司层面的审批（实体的FIRB审批和国内备案），并须满足业主的SOCI风险管理义务。与此同时，集团的排放数据必须达到调查所设定的标准。
:::

## [Smart meters]{.en}[智能水表]{.zh}

::: {.en}
**A meter used for billing needs NMI pattern approval, which takes about 12 months. Plumbing and drinking-water standards apply on top.**

::: tw
| Approval | Body | What it covers | Time and cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pattern approval (NMI R 49) | National Measurement Institute | Any meter type used for trade, i.e. billing \[91\] | About 12 months; about A\$40,000 per meter family, less if NMI accepts China lab results \[27\] [to verify]{.verify} |
| AS 3565.1 | Standards Australia, via certifier | Meter performance and construction | Certified alongside WaterMark \[27\] |
| AS/NZS 4020 and WaterMark | WaterMark certifier | Products in contact with drinking water; plumbing products | About A\$25,000 in the first year, then A\$3,000–6,000 a year \[27\] |
:::

A non-billing pilot meter does not measure for trade, so it should not need pattern approval [to verify]{.verify}. That lets a pilot start before approval (Report 6.3).
:::

::: {.zh}
**用于计费的水表需要NMI型式批准，约需12个月。此外还须满足管道和饮用水标准。**

::: tw
| 审批 | 机构 | 适用范围 | 时间与费用 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 型式批准（NMI R 49） | 国家计量院（NMI） | 所有用于贸易结算（即计费）的水表型号 \[91\] | 约12个月；每个系列约4万澳元，若NMI采信国内实验室结果则更低 \[27\] [待核实]{.verify} |
| AS 3565.1 | 澳洲标准协会，经认证机构 | 水表性能和结构 | 与WaterMark一并认证 \[27\] |
| AS/NZS 4020及WaterMark | WaterMark认证机构 | 接触饮用水的产品；管道产品 | 首年约2.5万澳元，此后每年3,000–6,000澳元 \[27\] |
:::

非计费试点水表不用于贸易计量，因此应不需要型式批准 [待核实]{.verify}。这样可以在获批前开展试点（报告6.3）。
:::
